2609.10253.title: DiSCo: A Distribution-First Steering and Cultural Prior Evaluation Framework for Measuring Cultural Preference Bias in LLMs
2609.10253.paper_summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in globally used assistants, yet their default choices in culturally grounded everyday situations can systematically favour some cultures over others, affecting localisation, user trust, and equitable behaviour. Existing cultural benchmarks evaluate accuracy against a single "correct" answer, making it difficult to characterise an LLM's cultural preference prior when multiple culturally grounded responses are all valid; they also conflate default preferences with context-driven adaptation. We propose DiSCo, a distribution-first forced-choice evaluation framework that isolates default cultural priors and tests steerability via a four-level context gradient (C0--C3). Using DiSCo-Bench (304 items) derived from BLEnD spanning 12 cultures, we evaluate six diverse instruction-tuned LLMs. Default priors are heavily concentrated, with UK and US together absorbing approximately 35\% of all selections despite representing only 2 of 12 cultures. Most critically, prompt-based steering consistently widens the selection gap between high- and low-resource cultures, and injecting explicit cultural facts produces negligible distributional disruption, confirming that cultural preference bias cannot be resolved through prompt-based personalisation alone.
2609.10253.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型（LLMs）越來越多地被應用於全球使用的助手中，但它們在文化根植的日常情境中的預設選擇可能系統性地偏向某些文化，影響本地化、用戶信任和公平行為。現有的文化基準評估準確性是針對單一的「正確」答案，這使得在多個文化根植的回應都是有效的情況下，難以表徵LLM的文化偏好；它們還將預設偏好與基於上下文的適應混淆。我們提出了DiSCo，一個以分佈為先的強制選擇評估框架，該框架隔離預設文化先驗並通過四級上下文梯度（C0--C3）測試可引導性。使用DiSCo-Bench（304項目），該項目源自BLEnD，涵蓋12種文化，我們評估了六種不同的指令調整LLM。預設先驗高度集中，英國和美國的選擇約佔所有選擇的35\%，儘管它們僅代表12種文化中的2種。最關鍵的是，基於提示的引導始終擴大了高資源文化和低資源文化之間的選擇差距，而注入明確的文化事實幾乎不會產生分佈性擾動，這確認了文化偏好偏見不能僅通過基於提示的個性化來解決。
